title: Playing with Ambrose's band
summary: Barnes recalls his first work with Ambrose, who played violin, and the guitar and bass players in that band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, that was guitar. And, uh, Rochon T played, uh, bass. And Gilles, he played bass, uh, guitar. Gilles Duvarny did.
He played guitar? Yeah. And, uh, when you first went out with Ambrose, what did he play at that time?
Well, I first went out with Ambrose then, he was playing, uh, violin. Uh-huh. Yeah, he was playing violin during that time.
And who did he have in his band?

Well, let's see, now you know what I mean? Well, it's been such a time ago, it's pretty tough to get that together. Well, uh, let's see who we got that. We had Ambrose, we had a fella called, uh, Johnny Pridons. And, uh, let's see, Ambrose, Johnny Pridons, that was a bass player too. Uh-huh. And sometimes T. Rochon, and sometimes, uh, uh, his boy Gilles Duvarny, ghetto. Uh-huh. Then we had this other one who used to play ghetto with us at times, uh, uh, T-Bar Francis. Is he any relation to Albert Francis?
No, I don't think it's any relation to Albert Francis.
No, I don't think it's any relation to Albert at all, I don't think. Not, not Conor Mano anymore. Uh-huh. No, I don't think.
Did Gilles Duvarny have his own band too?
